text:
PagerDuty Bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident fired for service=runtime-autoscaler, urgency=high. Trigger: queue_length > 100000 for 2m. Pager: oncall primary.

Infra Bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4273. Escalation policy: runtime-autoscale-escalation.

Jamie (oncall): acked. I'm on it, looking at queue metrics now.

Ravi: seeing a big spike in prefix requests from a handful of clients, 400k RPS burst -> queue depth jumped. Autoscaler hasn't increased replicas in 6m.

Sarah: rg the autoscaler metrics: controller reporting desired_replicas=8, actual_replicas=8, max_replicas=8 (hit config max). Cloud quota shows GPU quota is fine but the autoscaler max config capped at 8.

Matt: +1. Also seeing many inflight requests with KV cache misses; per-token latency spiked. Customer-facing lat p95 up from 120ms -> 1.8s, error rate 502s on downstream workers.

Jamie (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) bump autoscaler max to 30 (manual override) 2) enable emergency pool (dedicated burst nodes) 3) enable fallback model variant (cpu-quantized) for non-SL tier 4) apply rate-limit for highest-volume client. Who can run the scale command?

Ravi: I can run it. Running:
```
# scale override
kubectl patch hpa/autoscaler-runtime -n prod --type='merge' -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":30}}'
```

Ravi: patch applied. HPA controller shows target=30 but new nodes need ~2m to provision. K8s events show cloud provider launching instances.

Infra Bot: Noted: provisioning 10 GPU instances in us-west-2. ETA ~150s.

Sarah: meanwhile I'm flipping the routing rule for non-SL customers to a cheaper model variant to reduce token cost and processing time. Patch:
```
redwood-router update-route --route /generate --model rdx-small-quant --cond "customer_tier!=sl"
```

Matt: routing change applied. Non-SL p95 latency dropped immediately by ~40%. Good quick win.

Jamie (oncall): any way to drain backlog faster? Maybe spawn offline workers to pop the queue parallelly?

Ravi: starting emergency worker job to process queue in parallel (stateless consumer). Command:
```
./tools/queue-consumer --concurrency=64 --mode=burst --limit=50000
```

Ravi: worker started, consuming backlog. Queue size: 118k -> 72k within 90s.

Matt: observing error pattern: a small percentage of requests are being retried by upstream SDKs; that amplifies load. We should contact the top 3 customers and advise temporary throttle.

Jamie (oncall): I've DM'd account-eng for the top clients. @eng-platform can you also look into autoscaler logic — it didn't consider queue_length as a scaling metric, only CPU. We should add queue_length and avg_latency signals to prevent repeats.

eng-platform: on it, creating a PR to add a custom metric adapter. Quick patch in place to test, but needs follow-up for canary rollout.

PagerDuty Bot: Incident acknowledged by Jamie. Escalation stage 2 scheduled in 12m if no complete.

Sarah: provisioning completed, node counts increase to 22. New serving capacity coming online. Latency trending down.

Ravi: backlog now 9k and dropping. Error rate returning to baseline.

Jamie (oncall): summary so far: root cause = sudden traffic burst + client-side retries + autoscaler configured with only CPU-based scaling + hard max=8. Immediate mitigations taken: manual max bump -> nodes provisioned, emergency workers drained backlog, non-SL routing to faster model, rate-limit applied to heavy clients. Impact: p95 latency and 502s increased for ~12m, some customers saw degraded generation times.

Matt: postmortem action items (create tickets): - remove hard cap or set higher sensible default + autoscaler scale-to-zero guardrails - add queue_length metric and latency to autoscale policies - implement client-level adaptive rate limit and backoff guidance - automated emergency pool playbook + runbooks - alert tuning: avoid pages for short-lived bursts under Xs

Jamie (oncall): assigning tasks: Ravi -> runbook for manual scale and emergency worker steps. Sarah -> routing/fallback variant playbook. Eng-platform -> autoscaler metric PR and canary plan. Matt -> customer comms + who was affected.

Ravi: opened follow-up tickets: RW-9813 (runbook), RW-9814 (emergency-worker), RW-9815 (autoscaler-metrics).

Jamie (oncall): handing off to oncall secondary @Matt for overnight monitoring. I'll escalate to on-call lead in 30m with final status. Closing pager if metrics stable.

PagerDuty Bot: Incident status updated: acknowledged -> resolved (auto) after 45m. Incident INC-2026-4273 closed.

Matt: leaving a short note in #postmortems and creating a draft PM for execs. Thanks team. :heart:

Sarah: add monitoring dashboard widget for queue_length and a synthetic that simulates burst to test autoscaler.

Jamie (oncall): final note: customer-impact window was ~12m, top clients affected: corp-alpha (rate-limited), fastchat-inc (latency). Follow-ups required for compensation? assigning to accounts.

(End of thread)
